# alpen

A React map of every Austrian/German Alpine Club hut, plus an offline-computed hut-to-hut hiking
graph, built entirely on public third-party APIs — no backend of our own.

- `huts/` — the React/Vite/Leaflet map app. Fetches hut data live from the Alpenverein
  "Bettencheck" APIs, plus static files generated by `pipeline/`.
- `pipeline/` — offline precompute pipeline (OSM trail data → hut-to-hut routing graph +
  elevation), orchestrated as a [doit](https://pydoit.org) task DAG. Writes into `data/`
  (gitignored); outputs get copied into `huts/public/data/` for the app to serve statically.
- `docs/` — data source reference (`alpenverein-api.md`) and pipeline design rationale
  (`osm-trail-pipeline.md`).

Full details: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (app architecture), `pipeline/CLAUDE.md` +
`pipeline/README.md` (pipeline internals).

## Running the app

```bash
cd huts
npm install
npm run dev
```

The app fetches Alpine Club hut data live at runtime — no setup needed for that. It also fetches
static files from `huts/public/data/` (`stations.geojson`, `parking.geojson`, and, for the
opt-in `#graph` route, `huts.geojson`/`trails.pmtiles`/`hut-edges.pmtiles`/`hut-edge-stats.json`).
**Those files aren't checked into git** (see `.gitignore`) — on a fresh clone `huts/public/data/`
is empty and those requests 404 until you've run the pipeline below at least once and copied its
output in. `npm run build` / `npm run lint` / `npm run preview` are also available (see
`huts/package.json`).

## Reproducing the data pipeline

Everything the pipeline needs to reproduce its output is either in this repo (tracked code +
`pipeline.config.json` as the single source of hyperparameters) or fetched fresh from documented
public sources (Geofabrik OSM extracts, Copernicus/Austria/Bavaria DEM tiles, the Alpenverein
ArcGIS hut layer) — nothing hand-tuned or undocumented sits outside version control. `data/` (raw
downloads + generated outputs) is entirely gitignored and disposable: delete it and rerun the
pipeline to get back to the same place, modulo upstream sources changing over time.

**One-time environment setup** — the pipeline needs `osmium-tool` + a few natively-compiled
Python packages that aren't reliably available via plain `pip`, so it uses a dedicated
conda-forge env, `alpen-osm`, managed via [pixi](https://pixi.sh): `pipeline/pixi.toml` +
`pipeline/pixi.lock` are the tracked env manifest, so `pixi install` reproduces the exact same env
for everyone, no imperative setup commands to copy-paste. On Linux, macOS, or WSL:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh   # one-time, installs the pixi CLI itself
cd pipeline
pixi install                                  # reads pixi.toml/pixi.lock, builds the env
pixi run osmium --version   # sanity check: should print "osmium version ..."
```

`pixi run <cmd>` runs `<cmd>` inside the env (or `pixi shell` once to activate it for the rest of
the session). `tippecanoe` (needed for vector-tile builds) is in `pixi.toml` too and has
conda-forge builds for linux-64/osx-64/osx-arm64, so it's just another package in the same env on
those platforms — no extra step.

**Native Windows** (not WSL) isn't a supported `pixi` platform here, since `tippecanoe` has no
Windows conda-forge build — it needs a one-time WSL micromamba env just for `tippecanoe`
(`build_trail_tiles.py` detects Windows and shells out to it automatically via
`lib.pipeline.run_tippecanoe()`) — full commands in `pipeline/README.md` → "Setup". If you're
reading this from inside WSL already, ignore the Windows path entirely and use the instructions
above directly.

Full setup rationale: `pipeline/README.md` → "Setup".

**Running it** — the pipeline is a [doit](https://pydoit.org) task graph
(`pipeline/dodo.py`), one task per processing step, wired together by real file
dependencies/outputs so `doit` only reruns what's actually stale:

```bash
cd pipeline
pixi run doit list                # see every task + up-to-date status, without running anything
pixi run doit info <task>          # see *why* a task would (not) run
pixi run doit                       # run the full DAG, idempotently
pixi run doit <task> [<task> ...]  # run just one/some tasks (+ their stale deps)
```

**Read `pipeline/README.md` before running anything** — it documents every task, every
`pipeline.config.json` hyperparameter, and known-expensive steps (`build_hut_graph` measured at
~4.1 hours for the current AT+Bavaria scope; see `data/timings.jsonl` for real numbers as scope
grows). The last task, `copy_public_data`, copies every output straight into
`huts/public/data/` — that's the step that makes the app's static files reappear after a fresh
pipeline run.

## Reproducibility notes

- **Single source of hyperparameters**: every tunable (region list, trail tag filter, graph
  `max-edge-km`/`max-snap-m`, DEM provider/thresholds, tile zoom ranges) lives in
  `pipeline/pipeline.config.json`, read by every script — never hardcoded per-script. Changing it
  and rerunning `doit` reproducibly regenerates only what depends on the changed value.
- **No manual/undocumented steps**: the one genuinely manual piece is copying pipeline output into
  `huts/public/data/` — automated by the `copy_public_data` doit task, not a hand step anymore.
- **Timing is tracked, not guessed**: `pipeline/lib/timing.py` appends real per-phase durations to
  `data/timings.jsonl` on every run of an instrumented step, so "is this still fast enough as
  scope grows" is answered from data.
- **Raw sources are pinned by URL, not by hand-downloaded files**: `pipeline.config.json`'s
  `regions[].url` / DEM provider config are the only place an external source is named; rerunning
  `01-download-extracts`-equivalent (`doit download_extracts`) re-fetches from those exact URLs.
